children: Morgan Stanley, the investment-banking and wealth-management company

, led Accelevation's $540 million IPO alongside JPMorgan, according to Reuters, while its shares traded at $190.765, down approximately 1% on September 30. The AI-infrastructure supplier priced below its proposed range. AI demand may draw a crowd, but investors still want the right price.

According to Reuters, Accelevation sold 30 million shares at $18 each, below its initial $20-to-$24 range. The company issued 10 million shares, while affiliated shareholders sold the other 20 million. That puts gross proceeds to the company at $180 million before fees and expenses. The remaining $360 million went to selling shareholders.

For Morgan Stanley, the deal adds underwriting business, although its fee allocation was not disclosed. The valuation graphic puts its shares 6.81% above the $178.60 GF Value estimate, suggesting a modest premium rather than an obvious bargain. The IPO offers another useful signal: investors will fund AI infrastructure, but sellers cannot count on the theme alone to support their asking price.

title: Morgan Stanley Stocks Fall as AI IPO Prices Below Range
